title: Playground onramp: rapid experiment runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a short, working runbook for the interactive playground onramp — designed as a 30–90 minute hands-on experiment kit for new SDK adopters and internal demos. The goal: let an engineer get meaningful signals (latency, token cost, simple QA) from a tiny prototype without deep infra setup.

Audience:
- New integrators (engineers/PMs) trying Redwood SDKs for the first time.
- SEs running a short demo with a customer.
- Internal engineers sanity-checking SDK ergonomics or telemetry.

How to use this doc:
- Follow the three labs (quick, guided, deep) in order.
- Each lab has: objective, success criteria, commands/snippets, telemetry to capture, and two common failure modes.
- Notes/TODOs and bake-off matrix at the bottom. Treat this as a living notebook.

Lab A — Quick smoke (5–10m)
Objective: Make a single generation request from the browser SDK (JS) and render a streaming result.
Success criteria:
- Minimal code run in <10 minutes.
- Streaming tokens appear in the UI within 300–500ms of request start (on hosted).
- SDK emits one telemetry event with request_id and latency_ms.
Snippets (JS, minimal):
- npm i @redwood/sdk-playground (local stub OK)
- sample code:
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-lite', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize this: "T-shirt backlog"' }] })
  stream.on('token', t => appendTokenToUI(t))
  await stream.done()
Telemetry probes:
- Metric: playground.requests.count (tags: sdk=js, lab=quick)
- Histogram: playground.request.latency_ms
- Trace: playground.request.trace_id -> span: sdk.stream.start -> sdk.stream.end
Common failures:
- 401: missing key -> show instructions to set RW_KEY locally (env var or secrets).
- CORS fail: dev env misconfigured -> quick fix: use local reverse proxy (example command in appendix).

Lab B — Guided integration (20–30m)
Objective: Wire server-side SDK (Python/Node) to call a prompt template and save embeddings for search. Covers: batching, rate limit handling, and predictable costs.
Success criteria:
- Endpoint returns synthesis + embedding id in one request.
- Batching engaged (see metric playground.batch.size > 1 at peak).
- Cost estimate computed using tokenStats helper in SDK.
Checklist:
- Install runtime SDK and sample app (repo link in linked_artifacts).
- Load sample dataset (10 short docs).
- Run a script that issues 50 chat+embed hybrid requests at 1rps to surface batching behavior.
Sample curl (server side):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/combine -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -d '{"prompt": "Extract bullets", "docs": [..] }'
Telemetry to capture:
- playground.embed.calls.count, playground.chat.calls.count
- playground.batch.size distribution (should have >1 during bursts)
- cost.estimate.tokens and cost.estimate.usd (approx)
Failure modes:
- Silent throttling: SDK should surface 429 with backoff hints. Add note: if you see continuous 500s, enable verbose logging (SDK flag RW_DEBUG=1).
- Quality regression: embed model mismatch — reference model-matrix in Confluence and fallback policy recommended (auto-fallback to redwood-embed-compact)

Lab C — Canary + Rollback simulation (30–60m)
Objective: Exercise rollout semantics in Redwood Console (canary -> 20% -> 100%) and test graceful fallback when variant unavailable. Good for platform teams.
Success criteria:
- Canary rollout triggers at least one request routed to variant B.
- Upgrade causes no more than 2x the baseline error rate for 5 minutes.
- Automatic rollback triggers on errors > 5% and routes to fallback model within 30s.
Steps (high level):
- Create two model configs (stable, try) in console UI -> create canary policy (20% traffic).
- Launch a synthetic traffic job (see small script in repo).
- Observe per-route error rate and latency in console traces.
Telemetry and gates:
- per_route.errors.rate -> canary.errors.percent
- rollout.events: canary.start, canary.adjust, canary.rollback
- alert: rollout.regression (email/Slack) if error_rate > 5% for 5min
Troubleshooting:
- If canary not receiving traffic: check smart routing tag constraints (region, tier) — often mis-set to eu-west only.
- If fallback not invoked: confirm fallback model is compatible (same input schema).

Appendix — Small recipes & helper commands
Local reverse proxy (dev only):
  npx http-server -p 8080 &
  # proxy rule using local dev server: see /scripts/dev-proxy.js in repo
Script to generate synthetic traffic (node):
  node scripts/synth-requests.js --rate=5 --duration=60 --route=/v1/chat
Quick checks to run when something is flaky:
- env: echo $RW_KEY | wc -c (expected > 10 chars)
- curl -v to endpoint to inspect headers
- SDK: export RW_DEBUG=1 and repro small request; look for `x-rw-request-id` in responses

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we want a separate tiny Docker image for the guided lab that bundles the dataset + sample app? (pros: reproducible; cons: heavier for SE demos)
- Add a short video (2–3m) showing the three labs executed end-to-end; decide keeper: Diego/Maya to prototype.
- Telemetry: should we pre-create Grafana dashboard panels for the playground metrics? (low-effort templated dashboard would be helpful)

Experiment matrix (quick view):
- Variables: SDK language (js, py, go), deployment mode (hosted, dedicated), model size (lite, base, full), network (local, cloud)
- Metrics captured: first_token_latency_ms, request_p90_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens, batch_size_avg, errors_percent

Notes on style and UX friction observed during previous runs:
- Copy/paste friction: keys and sample envs often mis-named. Standardize on RW_KEY and document both local/test tokens and prod onboarding.
- Error messaging: unify 429 vs 503 messaging in SDK; prefer actionable text: "retry after Xs" or "contact SE@redwood".

Contacts & next steps:
- Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-devexp) — iterate this doc into final lab package
- Action: Diego to sketch Docker lab by 2025-02-09
- Action: Maya to add Grafana dashboard template PR (GH#repo/playground-dash)

This document intentionally informal; please add quick fixes and short snippets here rather than a long PR. Use the linked artifacts for canonical references.
